clue.text: Noble novelist hands around exotic hardcore

indicators.note: around places the two hands on either side of the jumbled word

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two hands

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange or unfamiliar, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocratic author passes round some unusual and explicit material.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is a best-selling British novelist who sits in the House of Lords. The hands are left and right, not a pair of card players or workers, and 'exotic' and 'around' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey Archer, a British peer since 1992, writes best-selling thrillers, so he is both a nobleman and an author.

clue.text: Place one in biblical plague finally departed

indicators.note: finally departed says the last letter of the insect has gone away

parts.note: the eighth plague of Egypt in Exodus was a swarm of locusts, so one of them is a locust

explanation.surface: Someone who lived through a scriptural pestilence has at last left a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally departed' removes the last letter, T, from LOCUST; 'Place' is a noun here, not an instruction to put something somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: in mathematics and formal writing it is the position or site where something is found.

clue.text: Again adjust the bottom line?

parts.note: the rear is the backside, the bottom
a range is a line, as of mountains or of products

explanation.surface: An accountant tweaks the profit figure once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bottom line' of the accounts splits in two: the bottom is one piece and line another.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to put things in a new order is to alter their set-up a second time.

clue.text: Government work isn't about to be held in respect

indicators.note: to be held in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for respect

parts.note: admiration is high regard, respect

indicators.note: about suggests the letters being thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A complaint that civil service jobs are not going to be esteemed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in respect' reads as one phrase, but 'to be held in' is the container signal and respect a separate word; 'about' is the jumbling signal, not a wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym pair: it names both the running of public affairs and the paperwork that running involves.

clue.text: Conservative performing well? Shut up!

parts.note: an act that is on is performing on stage
fine means well, as in feeling fine

explanation.surface: A Tory politician doing nicely is rudely told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' is not a call for silence but means to lock away.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to pen someone in or imprison them is to shut them up.

clue.text: Good time to split tip with fiancée?

indicators.note: to split says the two short pieces break the word for tip in two

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A suitable moment to share the gratuity with one's bride-to-be.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip is the point of something, not a gratuity, and 'to split' tells you it is broken open rather than shared.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive example: someone who has a wife-to-be has promised to marry.

clue.text: Idiot one battered in a chippy outside Lima

indicators.note: outside places the fish round the letter

parts.note: a chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop, where cod is fried in batter
Lima is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for L

explanation.surface: A fool gets beaten up in a fish-and-chip shop on the edge of the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps COD round L. 'Battered' is coated in batter, not beaten; a chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an insult for a dull, stupid person.

clue.text: Plane, going up, or going down?

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading upwards or downwards gives the same letters, so the word is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An aircraft that may be climbing or descending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up, or going down' says the entry reads the same in both directions in the grid; the plane is a flat surface, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in geometry and carpentry: a flat, even surface.

clue.text: French bums giving voice to Irish songs?

indicators.note: giving voice to means the Irish songs are spoken, and the sound is what matters

parts.note: Derry airs: tunes from the Northern Irish city of Derry, as in the Londonderry Air, the melody of Danny Boy

explanation.surface: Parisian layabouts belting out ballads from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving voice to' makes the songs a matter of sound: 'Derry airs' said out loud. The bums are bottoms, not tramps.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for backsides, borrowed into English as a polite euphemism.

clue.text: Helpful folk song a radio mast broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast in its old sense means scattered, as seed is, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handy traditional tune is transmitted from a wireless aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters the letters of SONG A RADIO MAST. 'folk song' reads as one phrase but 'folk' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Gospel parable: people who stop to assist strangers in need.

clue.text: A couple of guys and I shot a singer in ny

definitions.text: I shot a singer in ny

parts.note: a chap is one guy, an informal word for a fellow
a man is the other guy

explanation.surface: Two fellows and the speaker took a photograph of a vocalist in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like photography but is literal: Mark David Chapman shot John Lennon in New York in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Mark David, John Lennon's killer, who fired on the former Beatle outside the Dakota building.

clue.text: One cutting a record or disc in Cleveland?

indicators.note: in places the round letter inside the president's first name

parts.note: Grover Cleveland was twice president of the United States
the letter O is shaped like a disc

explanation.surface: Somebody making an LP or single in an Ohio city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside GROVER. Cleveland is the US president Grover, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or person that makes the spiral channel in vinyl is literally this.

clue.text: Running well, having eaten tons at home

indicators.note: having eaten says the water source has swallowed the other two pieces

parts.note: a well is a spring, a source of water
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone jogs comfortably after a huge meal in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running well' reads as one phrase, but well is a noun, the water source, and 'having eaten' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of the activity: moving on foot at top speed.

clue.text: Some remodel high-rises in an Asian city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people are refurbishing tower blocks somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: India's capital territory, one of the largest urban areas on the continent.

clue.text: Short of millions, one retiring star …

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the star is written backwards

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star

explanation.surface: A celebrity bowing out is a few million pounds down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' is a preposition meaning without; 'retiring' is going backwards, not leaving the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a preposition: lacking, with something taken away.

clue.text: Injured pal medics lost for a while?

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doctors could not find a hurt friend for some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' damages the letters of PAL MEDICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put down in the wrong spot is mislaid temporarily rather than gone for good.

clue.text: … Worried over a nude undertaking

indicators.note: worried means agitated or disturbed, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a project involving nakedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' disturbs the letters of OVER A NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an enterprise or attempt requiring effort.

clue.text: Surgery ready for business about ten to one?

indicators.note: about wraps the word for trading round the other piece

parts.note: a shop that is open is ready for business
ten to one is an example of a ratio, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: The doctor's office opens its doors at roughly 12.50.
explanation.walkthrough: A surgery is the British word for a doctor's consulting room, which makes 'ready for business' feel literal; 'ten to one' is odds, not a clock time, and 'about' is the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a medical procedure in which a patient is cut open.

clue.text: Curse weapon jammed by damage from use

indicators.note: jammed by says the other piece is wedged inside the weapon

parts.note: a sword is a weapon
wear is the gradual damage that use causes, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: Damn the gun that has seized up through overuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jammed by' suggests a gun that will not fire, but it only says one word is wedged inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an oath or expletive.

clue.text: Public speech to air on outrageous …

indicators.note: outrageous means wild and beyond normal bounds, so the letters run wild

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shocking address is about to be put out on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' reorders the words before it; the dots only link the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a formal address delivered to an audience.

clue.text: … Complaint I'd raised on mains energy

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the two letters are written upwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
the main is a poetic word for the open sea, so mains are seas
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A grumble the speaker made about the electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ID into DI. The mains are oceans, not the household supply, and the complaint is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an illness or ailment.

clue.text: When gulping half of water ice helps?

indicators.note: gulping says the word for when swallows the other piece

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: half of takes three of the six letters of the frozen dessert, here the second three

parts.note: a sorbet is a water ice

explanation.surface: Swallowing a partly melted frozen dessert gives some relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water ice' is one thing, a frozen dessert, so 'half of' applies to its synonym and not to the word water; 'gulping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym, usually of assisting in wrongdoing: aids and encourages.

clue.text: Bar supplier's inventory including ultimate in fizz

indicators.note: including puts the single letter inside the word for inventory

parts.note: an inventory is a list of stock

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A wholesaler's stock sheet for a pub lists the very best champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts Z, the 'ultimate in' fizz, inside LIST. The bars are bars of music, which a composer provides.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz, the Hungarian composer, wrote music, which is divided into measures.

clue.text: Feeling on edge? Take time out for son!

indicators.note: out for says one letter leaves and another takes its place

parts.note: tense means nervous, on edge
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An anxious parent is told to set aside a few hours for their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take time out for son' swaps the T of TENSE for S. 'Feeling on edge' reads as one phrase but splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an impression or awareness of something.

clue.text: Attacker giving trouble to soldier on dope

indicators.note: on says the first two pieces are added to the end of the third

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'
a soldier is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A mugger bothers a serviceman who is high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' attaches AIL and ANT to the end of ASS. The dope is a fool, not a drug, and the soldier an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who assaults another.

clue.text: A rough path's to follow after Republican gets in

indicators.note: gets in says the single letter enters the word for follow

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Hard times are expected once the GOP candidate is elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts R inside TAIL. The rough path is a literal track, not a difficult period.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an unpaved track through countryside.

clue.text: Dessert tin I left resting atop rolls

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: rolls means turns over, so the three pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: something resting atop another is on it

explanation.surface: A pudding container the speaker put down on top of the bread buns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' is a verb, turning over everything from 'I' to 'atop' as a single run, giving NOLI after the tin.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Sicilian fried pastry tubes filled with sweet ricotta.

clue.text: Coffee sailor found in Africa, not France

indicators.note: found in places the sailor inside what remains of the continent
not says the letter for France is absent from the continent's name

parts.note: F is the international vehicle registration code for France
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman came across a hot drink on one continent rather than in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the letter for France from the continent, leaving ARICA, and 'found in' then houses the sailor there.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the most widely grown species of the bean.

clue.text: Fast food one eats on a regular basis

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to fast is to restrict what one eats

definitions.text: food one eats on a regular basis
definitions.meaning: a person's habitual fare, what they normally eat

explanation.surface: Burgers and chips that somebody has all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' splits: fast is a verb on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to cut down on eating, and the habitual nourishment a person takes.

clue.text: A lean sun so unexpectedly odd in summer?

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters turn up in an order you would not expect

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weak, thin sun is a surprising thing to see in July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' reorders the letters of A LEAN SUN SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive example: weather out of keeping with the time of year, such as cold in July.
